_comment: This is the only file you edit to give Sophia a body.
One entry per physical thing you have wired up. Save the file, run
flash the board once, and Sophia can use it. No new code, ever, for a new
sensor or a new output - the firmware reads this table, it does not hard-code
name   what Sophia calls it. Lowercase, no spaces. Say it out loud first:
'turn on the desk lamp' works, 'toggle gpio5' does not.
type   digital_out | digital_in | analog_in | pwm_out | ultrasonic
pin    the GPIO number printed on the board, not the physical pin position.
pin2   only for ultrasonic (trig, echo). Ignored otherwise.
invert true if the hardware is active-low, which most relay boards are.
Sophia still says 'on' and means on; this flips it for her.
scale  optional multiplier for analog_in, so she reads 23.4 degrees
offset optional, applied after scale: value = raw * scale + offset
about  what it is, in plain words. This is what she is told it does, so
write it the way you would explain it to a person.
Delete the examples below. They are there to show the shape, and every one
of them is commented out by being inside _examples.

_examples.name: desk_lamp
_examples.about: The lamp on my desk, through a relay board.

_examples.name: status_led
_examples.about: An LED I use to show she is listening. 0-255.

_examples.name: desk_button
_examples.about: A push button wired to ground. Reads 1 while held down.

_examples.name: room_temp
_examples.about: Analog temperature sensor on the wall. Reads in degrees C.

_examples.name: doorway
_examples.about: Ultrasonic sensor pointed at the doorway. Reads distance in cm.
